```asm
    sub     sp, #0xC
    add     r5, r0, #0                      ; client
    ldr     r0, [r5, #0x28]
    add     r7, r1, #0                      ; battler (r1 is passed on unchanged)
    bl      Battle_GetSpriteSlot
    add     r6, r0, #0                      ; slot
    add     r0, r7, #0
    bl      Battler_FacingKind
    cmp     r0, #0
    beq     @@facing
    mov     r0, #2
@@facing:
    str     r0, [sp, #4]                    ; facing: 0 back (player's side), 2 front (foe)
    add     r0, r6, #0
    bl      BattleSprite_Get
    add     r4, r0, #0                      ; sprite
    ldr     r0, [r5, #0x28]
    add     r1, r7, #0
    bl      Battle_GetMonView
    add     r7, r0, #0                      ; MonView
    ldr     r0, =FaintState
    ldrb    r1, [r0, #1]                    ; state
    cmp     r1, #5
    bls     @@dispatch
    b       @@exit
@@dispatch:
    add     r1, r1, r1
    add     r1, pc
    ldrh    r1, [r1, #6]
    lsl     r1, r1, #16
    asr     r1, r1, #16
    add     pc, r1
@@table:
    .halfword @@state0 - @@table - 2
    .halfword @@state1 - @@table - 2
    .halfword @@state2 - @@table - 2
    .halfword @@state3 - @@table - 2
    .halfword @@state4 - @@table - 2
    .halfword @@state5 - @@table - 2

@@state0:                                   ; prepare; when ready: the faint cry (new), state 1
    add     r0, r5, #0
    add     r1, r6, #0
    mov     r2, #0
    mov     r3, #1
    bl      Faint_Prepare
    cmp     r0, #0
    beq     @@exit
    ldr     r2, [sp, #4]
    sub     r2, #1
    mov     r0, #FAINT_PAN
    mul     r2, r0                          ; pan: -117 back, +117 front
    ldrb    r0, [r7, #5]
    str     r0, [sp, #8]                    ; form
    mov     r0, #0
    str     r0, [sp, #4]                    ; delay 0
    ldrh    r1, [r7]                        ; species
    mov     r3, #CRY_VOLUME
    mov     r0, #HEAP_ID_BATTLE
    str     r0, [sp]                        ; heap
    mov     r0, #CRY_MODE_FAINT
    bl      Cry_Play
    mov     r1, #1
    b       @@set_state

@@state1:                                   ; wait for the cry; the faint sound (new); health box; state 2 or 3
    bl      Cry_IsPlaying
    cmp     r0, #0
    bne     @@exit
    ldr     r1, [sp, #4]
    sub     r1, #1
    mov     r0, #FAINT_PAN
    mul     r1, r0                          ; pan
    ldr     r0, =SEQ_SE_DP_POKE_DEAD3
    bl      PlaySEWithPan
    add     r0, r4, #0
    mov     r1, #ATTR_RAISE
    bl      Sprite_GetAttr
    mov     r1, #3
    cmp     r0, #0
    ble     @@state1_set
    mov     r1, #2                          ; raised: lower it first
@@state1_set:
    ldr     r0, =FaintState
    strb    r1, [r0, #1]
    ldr     r0, [r5, #0x28]
    add     r1, r6, #0
    mov     r2, #0
    bl      Faint_HealthboxOut
    b       @@exit

@@set_state:                                ; r1 = the next state
    ldr     r0, =FaintState
    strb    r1, [r0, #1]
@@exit:
    mov     r0, #0
    add     sp, #0xC
    pop     {r4-r7, pc}

@@state2:                                   ; lower a raised sprite 8 px a frame; then state 3 at once
    add     r0, r4, #0
    mov     r1, #ATTR_RAISE
    bl      Sprite_GetAttr
    add     r5, r0, #0
    sub     r5, #8
    bpl     @@state2_set
    mov     r5, #0
@@state2_set:
    add     r0, r4, #0
    mov     r1, #ATTR_RAISE
    add     r2, r5, #0
    bl      Sprite_SetAttr
    cmp     r5, #0
    bne     @@exit
    ldr     r0, =FaintState
    mov     r1, #3
    strb    r1, [r0, #1]

@@state3:                                   ; draw only the part above the ground line; state 4
    mov     r0, #0
    str     r0, [sp]
    mov     r1, #(MONVIEW_GENDER >> 2)
    lsl     r1, r1, #2
    add     r1, #(MONVIEW_GENDER & 3)
    ldrb    r1, [r7, r1]                    ; gender
    ldrb    r3, [r7, #5]                    ; form
    ldr     r2, [sp, #4]                    ; facing
    ldrh    r0, [r7]                        ; species
    bl      Mon_GetSpriteYOffset
    mov     r3, #0x50
    sub     r0, r3, r0
    mov     r1, #0
    str     r0, [sp]
    add     r0, r4, #0
    add     r2, r1, #0
    bl      Sprite_SetPartialDraw
    mov     r1, #4
    b       @@set_state

@@state4:                                   ; slide down 8 px a frame until hidden; state 5
    add     r0, r4, #0
    mov     r1, #ATTR_Y
    mov     r2, #8
    bl      Sprite_AddAttr
    add     r0, r4, #0
    mov     r1, #ATTR_HEIGHT
    bl      Sprite_GetAttr
    add     r5, r0, #0
    sub     r5, #8
    bpl     @@state4_set
    mov     r5, #0
@@state4_set:
    add     r0, r4, #0
    mov     r1, #ATTR_HEIGHT
    add     r2, r5, #0
    bl      Sprite_SetAttr
    cmp     r5, #0
    bne     @@exit
    add     r0, r4, #0
    bl      Sprite_Delete
    mov     r1, #5
    b       @@set_state

@@state5:                                   ; wait for the health box; reset the state, done
    ldrb    r1, [r0]                        ; r0 = FaintState (from the dispatch)
    cmp     r1, #0
    bne     @@exit
    mov     r1, #0
    strb    r1, [r0, #1]
    add     sp, #0xC
    mov     r0, #1
    pop     {r4-r7, pc}

.pool
.endarea

.close
```

</details>

## battle-heal-hpbar-switched-out

**Battle: a Potion on a Pokémon that is forced out the same turn no longer freezes (Maxie gauntlet)**

- Kind: code
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-2314
- Source: `work/patches/battle-heal-hpbar-switched-out/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: in the second wave of Maxie's gauntlet at the top of the Lavender Town tower (the double battle
against Magmortar and Houndoom), using a Potion from the battle Bag on the Pokémon in battle can freeze the
game right after 'used the Potion!' (Discord report, 2026-10-07). It happens when Houndoom uses Roar in the
same turn and drags another Pokémon in: the healed Pokémon has already left the field when the Potion's
health bar is animated. Reproduced on melonDS 1.1 with the untouched Chinese ROM and with develop
(work/notes/melonds-retest_fix.md); DeSmuME keeps running. Real hardware is untested. Any healing item from
the Bag followed by a forced switch of that Pokémon in the same turn takes the same path.

Status: D-1337 says hack bugs are reported, not fixed. This fix is a user-approved exception to it (D-2314,
2026-10-09); other hack bugs stay report-only.

Technical: the hack's battle engine (overlay 14) computes the whole turn, then plays it back. The Potion's
playback command (handler 0x022053D0) calls 0x0222E024 with the healed Pokémon's id; that routine finds the
battler showing the Pokémon (0x02228740) from the party order after the whole turn. After Roar the Pokémon
is not on the field: the lookup returns 5, the battler-to-bar table (0x0224D134) maps it to health bar 0,
which a double battle never sets up, and the bar task's gauge drawing (0x02210C94) loads the bar's NULL
sprite pointer and reads address 0 (ldr r0, [r0] at 0x02210C9E). melonDS raises a data abort (abort LR
0x02210CA6) and the game hangs; DeSmuME reads address 0 and goes on. In a single battle the same lookup
picks the opponent's bar instead (no crash, a wrong bar animates).

**What (old → new):**

Old: battler lookup 5 (not on the field) -> health bar 0 (double) or the opponent's bar (single) ->
animation task on it -> NULL sprite read -> data abort.

New: 0x0222E024 checks the lookup: for 5 it writes that nonzero value to the command's done flag and returns
without a health-bar task, so the playback goes on with the next event; the bar of a Pokémon on the field
is animated exactly as before. The routine is re-laid in place (0x4C bytes, the same literal pool) to make
room: the handler passes the id byte in r0 as well ('ldr r0, [r3, #0x28]' -> 'lsr r0, r1, #0x18' at
0x022053E8; the routine never read the old r0), and the bar address G + 0x2AC + index * 0x3C is computed as
G + (index + 11) * 0x3C + 0x18. Not changed: the HP itself (the battle data already holds it), the order of
the turn, Roar, the other playback commands.

**Evidence:**

- D-2314: the user-approved exception to D-1337 for this fix (user request 2026-10-09: 'We want to fix these bugs, so for each issue create a worktree per issue, and use a separate subagent to fix, test and review.')
- work/notes/melonds-retest_fix.md: reproduction on melonDS 1.1 (Chinese ROM and develop), the abort, the call chain, the party order after Roar, the before/after runs
- Runtime: emu_harness.py fixes --case battle-heal-hpbar-switched-out (scenario battle-heal: emu_battle_heal.py, a Potion on the lead in a trainer battle where the opponent can only use Roar; run on the build and on one without this fix)

**Touches:**

- `overlay14+0x4C08` (RAM 0x022053E8) `battle-heal-hpbar-switched-out-caller`: 2 bytes, was `6A98`
- `overlay14+0x2D844` (RAM 0x0222E024) `battle-heal-hpbar-switched-out-routine`: 76 bytes, was `B570 1C08 1C16 1C1D … (38 halfwords)`

**Disassembly snapshot:** [`battle-heal-hpbar-switched-out.listing`](battle-heal-hpbar-switched-out/battle-heal-hpbar-switched-out.listing) (every edit, old → new; `python3 work/tools/asmpatch.py listing --write battle-heal-hpbar-switched-out`)

**Source** (`work/patches/battle-heal-hpbar-switched-out/battle-heal-hpbar-switched-out.asm`, armips; the new bytes):

<details>
<summary>battle-heal-hpbar-switched-out.asm</summary>

```asm
; battle-heal-hpbar-switched-out - Battle: a healing item used on a Pokemon that is forced out later in the
; same turn (Roar, ...) no longer freezes the game (Maxie gauntlet, Lavender Town). D-2314 (user-approved
; exception to D-1337). Why and what: fix.toml next to this file; overview work/patches/FIXES.md;
; work/notes/melonds-retest_fix.md.
;
; The hack's battle engine (overlay 14) computes a whole turn first and then plays it back on the client.
; A Potion from the battle Bag queues the client command handled by BattleHeal_Cmd (0x022053D0): state 0
; calls BattleHeal_StartBar (0x0222E024, r1 = the healed Pokemon's id byte, r2 = HP, r3 = the command's done
; flag), state 1 waits for that flag. BattleHeal_StartBar looks up the battler that shows the Pokemon
; (0x02228740: battler 0-3, or 5 when the Pokemon is not on the field), turns it into a health-bar index
; (0x022156C4) and starts a task (0x0222DFE8) that animates that health bar and sets the done flag.
; The lookup reads the party order after the whole turn. When the same turn forces the healed Pokemon out
; (Houndoom's Roar in the gauntlet's second wave), it is no longer on the field: the lookup returns 5, the
; index table gives health bar 0, which a double battle never sets up, and the task's gauge drawing reads
; the bar's NULL sprite (ldr r0, [r0] at 0x02210C9E). melonDS 1.1 (and the hardware's protection unit)
; raise a data abort there and the game freezes on 'used the Potion!'; DeSmuME reads address 0 and goes on.
; In a single battle the same index points at the opponent's bar instead.
;
; The fix: when the lookup returns 5, BattleHeal_StartBar writes that nonzero value to the done flag and
; returns without a health-bar task (the Pokemon's bar is not on screen; it is drawn from its current HP when
; it comes back). To make room in place, the routine is re-laid: the caller passes the id in r0 (it was
; loaded into r1 and r0 was unused), and G + 0x2AC + index * 0x3C is computed as G + (index + 11) * 0x3C
; + 0x18. Every other step, its order, the task, its priority and the literal pool are unchanged.

.nds
.thumb
.include "../include/guards.inc"

.definelabel BattleHeal_Cmd,        0x022053D0   ; client command handler: state 0 start, state 1 wait
.definelabel BattleHeal_CmdLoadR0,  0x022053E8   ; ldr r0, [r3, #0x28] (r0 unused by the callee)  <- edit 1
.definelabel BattleHeal_StartBar,   0x0222E024   ; r1 = Pokemon id, r2 = HP, r3 = done flag      <- edit 2
.definelabel Battle_BattlerOfMon,   0x02228740   ; id -> battler 0-3, 5 = not on the field
.definelabel Battle_HealthbarIndex, 0x022156C4   ; battler -> health-bar index (table 0x0224D134)
.definelabel Healthbar_SetHpChange, 0x02210A64
.definelabel CreateSysTask,         0x0200DE74
.definelabel HealthbarHeal_Task,    0x0222DFE9   ; the bar animation task (Thumb)
.definelabel Battle_Global,         0x02255C74   ; -> G; health bars at G + 0x2AC, 0x3C bytes each

.open "overlay14.bin", 0x022007E0

; Edit 1: the handler passes the id byte in r0 as well (r1 holds id << 24 here).
.org BattleHeal_Cmd
    expect16_at 0x00, 0xB538    ; push  {r3-r5, lr}
    expect16_at 0x02, 0x1C0C    ; add   r4, r1, #0
    expect16_at 0x04, 0x1C03    ; add   r3, r0, #0
    expect16_at 0x06, 0x6820    ; ldr   r0, [r4]                state
    expect16_at 0x08, 0x2800    ; cmp   r0, #0
    expect16_at 0x0A, 0xD002    ; beq   state 0
    expect16_at 0x0C, 0x2801    ; cmp   r0, #1
    expect16_at 0x0E, 0xD00E    ; beq   state 1
    expect16_at 0x10, 0xE014    ; b     return 0
    expect16_at 0x12, 0x6811    ; ldr   r1, [r2]                Pokemon id (command argument 0)
    expect16_at 0x14, 0x255D    ; mov   r5, #0x5D
    expect16_at 0x16, 0x0609    ; lsl   r1, r1, #0x18
    expect16_at 0x1A, 0x012D    ; lsl   r5, r5, #4              done flag at +0x5D0
    expect16_at 0x1C, 0x6852    ; ldr   r2, [r2, #4]            HP (command argument 1)
    expect16_at 0x1E, 0x0E09    ; lsr   r1, r1, #0x18
    expect16_at 0x20, 0x195B    ; add   r3, r3, r5
    expect16_at 0x22, 0xF028    ; bl    BattleHeal_StartBar     (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x24, 0xFE17    ;                               (2/2)
.org BattleHeal_CmdLoadR0
.area 2
    expect16 0x6A98             ; ldr   r0, [r3, #0x28]
    lsr     r0, r1, #0x18
.endarea

; Edit 2: BattleHeal_StartBar, push through literal pool (0x4C bytes), re-laid with the not-on-field exit.
.org BattleHeal_StartBar
    expect32_at 0x00, 0x1C08B570    ; push {r4-r6, lr}; add r0, r1, #0
    expect32_at 0x04, 0x1C1D1C16    ; add r6, r2, #0; add r5, r3, #0
    expect32_at 0x08, 0xFB88F7FA    ; bl Battle_BattlerOfMon
    expect32_at 0x0C, 0xFB48F7E7    ; bl Battle_HealthbarIndex
    expect32_at 0x10, 0x680A490C    ; ldr r1, =Battle_Global; ldr r2, [r1]
    expect32_at 0x14, 0x008921AB    ; mov r1, #0xAB; lsl r1, r1, #2
    expect32_at 0x18, 0x213C1852    ; add r2, r2, r1; mov r1, #0x3C
    expect32_at 0x1C, 0x18544341    ; mul r1, r0; add r4, r2, r1
    expect32_at 0x20, 0x1C311C20    ; add r0, r4, #0; add r1, r6, #0
    expect32_at 0x24, 0xFD0CF7E2    ; bl Healthbar_SetHpChange
    expect32_at 0x28, 0x22FA1C20    ; add r0, r4, #0; mov r2, #0xFA
    expect32_at 0x2C, 0x210063A5    ; str r5, [r4, #0x38]; mov r1, #0
    expect32_at 0x30, 0x30237029    ; strb r1, [r5]; add r0, #0x23
    expect32_at 0x34, 0x48047001    ; strb r1, [r0]; ldr r0, =HealthbarHeal_Task
    expect32_at 0x38, 0x00921C21    ; add r1, r4, #0; lsl r2, r2, #2
    expect32_at 0x3C, 0xFF08F5DF    ; bl CreateSysTask
    expect32_at 0x40, 0x46C0BD70    ; pop {r4-r6, pc}; nop
    expect32_at 0x44, Battle_Global
    expect32_at 0x48, HealthbarHeal_Task
.area 0x4C
    push    {r4-r6, lr}
    add     r6, r2, #0              ; HP
    add     r5, r3, #0              ; done flag
    bl      Battle_BattlerOfMon     ; r0 = Pokemon id (edit 1)
    cmp     r0, #5
    beq     @@not_on_field
    bl      Battle_HealthbarIndex
    add     r0, #11
    mov     r1, #0x3C
    mul     r0, r1
    ldr     r1, [@@global]
    ldr     r1, [r1]
    add     r4, r1, r0
    add     r4, #0x18               ; r4 = G + 0x2AC + index * 0x3C
    add     r0, r4, #0
    add     r1, r6, #0
    bl      Healthbar_SetHpChange
    str     r5, [r4, #0x38]         ; the task sets this flag when it ends
    mov     r1, #0
    strb    r1, [r5]
    mov     r0, #0x23
    strb    r1, [r4, r0]            ; task state 0
    ldr     r0, [@@task]
    add     r1, r4, #0
    mov     r2, #0xFA
    lsl     r2, r2, #2              ; priority 1000
    bl      CreateSysTask
    pop     {r4-r6, pc}
@@not_on_field:
    strb    r0, [r5]                ; done (5): the handler moves on, no bar to animate
    pop     {r4-r6, pc}
.align 4
@@global:
    .word   Battle_Global
@@task:
    .word   HealthbarHeal_Task
.endarea

.close
```

</details>

## battle-hit-sound

**Battles: a move that deals damage plays the hit sound again (normal, super effective, not very effective)**

- Kind: code
- Enabled: no
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-2342
- Source: `work/patches/battle-hit-sound/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: in battle you hear a move's animation but not the sound of the attack hitting (Discord, rc5: 'you
don't hear the noise of your attack hitting'; 'Pikachu's Electro Ball has no sound when the animation goes
off'). HeartGold plays a hit sound with every damaging hit, louder for a super-effective one and softer for a
not-very-effective one. The untouched Chinese hack never plays it, so this is a bug of the hack.

Status: D-1337 says hack bugs are reported, not fixed. This fix is a user-approved exception to it
(D-2342, 2026-10-09); other hack bugs stay report-only.

Status: disabled. Merged into develop on 2026-10-12 at the user's request as a separate, switched-off patch: the
standard build leaves it out (the Chinese behaviour is kept) and it is built only on request
(build.py --only battle-hit-sound).

Technical: the hack replaced HeartGold's battle code with its own engine in overlay 14, which drives the
screen with a list of commands. Command 8 (command table 0x0224ABC0, entry 8; BattleAct_MoveDamage,
0x02204CF0; 'command 8' in faint-waits-for-hp-bar too) shows a move's damage: arguments [target count, effectiveness class, move id, ...], per target a
battler id and the damage. It starts the target's blink and the HP-bar drain, but plays no sound, and no code
in the hack plays the hit sounds SEQ_SE_DP_KOUKA_H/L/M (1788/1789/1790; every overlay and arm9 searched, and
the PlaySE / sequence-start calls logged in battle). HeartGold plays them from battle command 215
(PlayMoveHitSoundEffect) through the client handler at US overlay12 0x0225B3D4: normal 1790, super
effective 1788, not very effective 1789. The effectiveness class of command 8 is 1 normal, 2 super effective,
3 not very effective (observed with the battle messages 2#74 / 2#75). HeartGold sends 0 (normal), 1 (not very
effective) or 2 (super effective) from the move's effectiveness flags only, so every damaging hit without an
effectiveness flag (fixed damage such as Seismic Toss or Dragon Rage, Future Sight) plays 1790; the hack sends
class 1 for those, so they match.

**What (old → new):**

Old: command 8 builds its target and damage lists, starts the blink and the HP bar; no sound.

New: step 0's list-building loop (overlay 14 0x02204D0E-0x02204D4F, 66 bytes) is rewritten more compactly,
and the bytes it frees call PlaySE (arm9 0x02005F5C) first: class 1 -> 1790 KOUKA_M, 2 -> 1788 KOUKA_H,
3 -> 1789 KOUKA_L, any other class -> no sound. The lists (target position from 0x02215704 for each battler
id's low byte, each damage's low halfword), their count and the registers and stack slots the unchanged code
after it uses are the same, so the blink and the HP bar run as before. One sound per command, also for a move
that hits several targets (by the command's one class: Surf on Mewtwo and Tyranitar plays only the super
effective sound; HeartGold plays one per target), and per hit of a multi-hit move. Not as in HeartGold: the sound is centred
(HeartGold pans it to the target's side; there is no room for that here). Not changed: move animations that
have no sound of their own (Electro Ball and the other hack-added moves listed in D-1598), the missing cry
when an opposing Pokemon faints, and every other command: a one-hit KO move (command 12) and a hit on a
substitute stay silent, although HeartGold plays the hit sound for them too (its move-damage subscript 2 and
substitute subscript 90 are the only US battle subscripts with command 215). As in HeartGold, residual
damage and a Pokemon hurting itself in its confusion (command 28) play no hit sound.

**Evidence:**

- D-2342: the user-approved exception to D-1337 for this fix (user request 2026-10-09: 'We want to fix these bugs, so for each issue create a worktree per issue, and use a separate subagent to fix, test and review.')
- work/notes/hit-sound_fix.md: the cause, the HeartGold reference, the rewrite and the emulator runs before and after
- Runtime: emu_harness.py fixes --case battle-hit-sound (scenario hitsound: Pikachu Lv50 uses Tackle on a wild Snorlax, Thunderbolt on a wild Gyarados and Tackle on a wild Onix; every sequence the game starts is logged; run on the build and on one without this fix, work/notes/emu_harness.md 'Fix scenarios')

**Touches:**

- `overlay14+0x452E` (RAM 0x02204D0E) `battle-hit-sound-step0`: 66 bytes, was `2000 9002 9801 2800 … (33 halfwords)`

**USA cross-checks** (`[[us_ref]]`, each checked against the USA ROM by `usref.py`, `check.py --full`):

- `US overlay12 0x0225B3D4` = `B570 1C06 1C0D 4812 2101 5C28 1C14 4208` (unique in the file): US overlay12 0x0225B3D4 is HeartGold's hit-sound client handler: by the effectiveness byte (data+1) it plays 1790 (0), 1788 (2) or 1789 (1) with PlaySEWithPan; the hack has no such code
- `US arm9 0x0200604C` = the Chinese ROM's 6 bytes at `arm9 0x02005F5C`: US arm9 0x0200604C is PlaySE(u16 seq); its first 6 bytes are the hack's PlaySE at 0x02005F5C (the calls after them differ only in their offsets)

**Disassembly snapshot:** [`battle-hit-sound.listing`](battle-hit-sound/battle-hit-sound.listing) (every edit, old → new; `python3 work/tools/asmpatch.py listing --write battle-hit-sound`)

**Source** (`work/patches/battle-hit-sound/battle-hit-sound.asm`, armips; the new bytes):

<details>
<summary>battle-hit-sound.asm</summary>

```asm
; battle-hit-sound - Battles: a damaging move plays the hit sound again (normal, super effective, not very
; effective). D-2342 (user-approved exception to D-1337).
; Why and what: fix.toml next to this file; overview work/patches/FIXES.md; work/notes/hit-sound_fix.md.
;
; The hack's battle engine (overlay 14) drives the screen with a list of commands. Command 8 (command
; table 0x0224ABC0, entry 8 = BattleAct_MoveDamage, 0x02204CF0) shows a move's damage: its
; arguments are [target count, type-effectiveness class, move id, ...] and per target a battler id and the
; damage (BattleClient +0x98 / +0x9C, 8 bytes apart). Step 0 builds the target and damage lists, starts the
; blink (0x0222EF1C) and the HP-bar drain (0x022013E0); step 1 waits. The effectiveness class is 1 normal,
; 2 super effective, 3 not very effective (observed: Thunderbolt on Gyarados 2 with 2#74, Tackle on Onix 3
; with 2#75, Tackle on Snorlax 1). Nothing in the handler plays a sound, and no code in the hack plays the
; hit sounds SEQ_SE_DP_KOUKA_H/L/M (1788/1789/1790). The untouched HeartGold plays one of them with every
; hit (battle command 215 -> client handler US overlay12 0x0225B3D4: normal 1790, super 1788, not very 1789).
;
; The fix rewrites step 0's list-building loop (0x02204D0E-0x02204D4F, 66 bytes) more compactly and uses
; the bytes it frees to play the hit sound for the class first: PlaySE(1786 + (class == 1 ? 4 : class)),
; i.e. 1 -> 1790 KOUKA_M, 2 -> 1788 KOUKA_H, 3 -> 1789 KOUKA_L; any other class plays nothing. The loop
; builds the same two lists (target object from 0x02215704 with the battler id's low byte, damage's low
; halfword) for the same count, and leaves the same registers for the unchanged code after it (0x02204D50:
; count at [sp+4], lists at sp+0x18 / sp+0x10, r7 = BattleClient). [sp+8] holds the remaining count
; instead of the index; [sp+0xC] is no longer used (both are scratch slots of this step only).

.nds
.thumb
.include "../include/guards.inc"

.definelabel PlaySE,                     0x02005F5C   ; arm9: PlaySE(u16 seq) (US arm9 0x0200604C)
.definelabel BattleAct_MoveDamage,       0x02204CF0   ; overlay 14, command 8: (client r0, step* r1, args* r2)
.definelabel BattleAct_MoveDamage_Step0, 0x02204D0E   ; step 0: build the lists  <- rewritten
.definelabel BattleAct_MoveDamage_Start, 0x02204D50   ; blink + HP bar, step++   (unchanged)
.definelabel BattleClient_GetMonObject,  0x02215704   ; (r0 = [client+0x28], r1 = battler id) -> object
.definelabel BattleBlink_Start,          0x0222EF1C   ; (objects*, count)
.definelabel BattleHpBar_Start,          0x022013E0   ; (client, objects*, damages*, count)

SEQ_SE_DP_KOUKA_BASE equ 1786                         ; + 2 = KOUKA_H 1788, + 3 = KOUKA_L 1789, + 4 = KOUKA_M 1790

.open "overlay14.bin", 0x022007E0

; Read-only guard: the handler's entry and dispatch, unchanged. r2 (args) is not touched before step 0.
.org BattleAct_MoveDamage
    expect16_at 0x00, 0xB5F8    ; push  {r3-r7, lr}
    expect16_at 0x02, 0xB08A    ; sub   sp, #0x28
    expect16_at 0x04, 0x1C07    ; add   r7, r0, #0              r7 = BattleClient
    expect16_at 0x06, 0x6810    ; ldr   r0, [r2]                args[0] = target count
    expect16_at 0x08, 0x9100    ; str   r1, [sp]                step*
    expect16_at 0x0A, 0x0400    ; lsl   r0, r0, #16
    expect16_at 0x0C, 0x0C00    ; lsr   r0, r0, #16
    expect16_at 0x0E, 0x9001    ; str   r0, [sp, #4]            count (u16)
    expect16_at 0x10, 0x1C08    ; add   r0, r1, #0
    expect16_at 0x12, 0x6800    ; ldr   r0, [r0]                step
    expect16_at 0x14, 0x2800    ; cmp   r0, #0
    expect16_at 0x16, 0xD002    ; beq   BattleAct_MoveDamage_Step0
    expect16_at 0x18, 0x2801    ; cmp   r0, #1
    expect16_at 0x1A, 0xD035    ; beq   0x02204D78              step 1: wait
    expect16_at 0x1C, 0xE03B    ; b     0x02204D86

; Read-only guard: what follows the rewritten part, which relies on [sp+4], sp+0x18, sp+0x10 and r7.
.org BattleAct_MoveDamage_Start
    expect16_at 0x00, 0x9901    ; ldr   r1, [sp, #4]
    expect16_at 0x02, 0xA806    ; add   r0, sp, #0x18           objects
    expect16_at 0x04, 0x0609    ; lsl   r1, r1, #24
    expect16_at 0x06, 0x0E09    ; lsr   r1, r1, #24
    expect16_at 0x08, 0xF02A    ; bl    BattleBlink_Start (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x0A, 0xF8E0    ;                         (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x0C, 0x9B01    ; ldr   r3, [sp, #4]
    expect16_at 0x0E, 0x1C38    ; add   r0, r7, #0
    expect16_at 0x10, 0x061B    ; lsl   r3, r3, #24
    expect16_at 0x12, 0xA906    ; add   r1, sp, #0x18           objects
    expect16_at 0x14, 0xAA04    ; add   r2, sp, #0x10           damages
    expect16_at 0x16, 0x0E1B    ; lsr   r3, r3, #24
    expect16_at 0x18, 0xF7FC    ; bl    BattleHpBar_Start (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x1A, 0xFB3A    ;                         (2/2)

; The edit: step 0's loop, rewritten, with the hit sound in front of it.
.org BattleAct_MoveDamage_Step0
.area BattleAct_MoveDamage_Start - BattleAct_MoveDamage_Step0
    expect16_at 0x00, 0x2000    ; mov   r0, #0
    expect16_at 0x02, 0x9002    ; str   r0, [sp, #8]            i = 0
    expect16_at 0x04, 0x9801    ; ldr   r0, [sp, #4]
    expect16_at 0x06, 0x2800    ; cmp   r0, #0
    expect16_at 0x08, 0xDD1B    ; ble   BattleAct_MoveDamage_Start
    expect16_at 0x0A, 0x9E02    ; ldr   r6, [sp, #8]
    expect16_at 0x0C, 0xAC06    ; add   r4, sp, #0x18
    expect16_at 0x0E, 0xAD04    ; add   r5, sp, #0x10
    expect16_at 0x10, 0x00B0    ; lsl   r0, r6, #2              loop: offset 8 * i
    expect16_at 0x12, 0x9003    ; str   r0, [sp, #0xC]
    expect16_at 0x14, 0x9903    ; ldr   r1, [sp, #0xC]
    expect16_at 0x16, 0x6AB8    ; ldr   r0, [r7, #0x28]
    expect16_at 0x18, 0x1879    ; add   r1, r7, r1
    expect16_at 0x1A, 0x3198    ; add   r1, #0x98
    expect16_at 0x1C, 0x6809    ; ldr   r1, [r1]                battler id
    expect16_at 0x1E, 0x0609    ; lsl   r1, r1, #24
    expect16_at 0x20, 0x0E09    ; lsr   r1, r1, #24
    expect16_at 0x22, 0xF010    ; bl    BattleClient_GetMonObject (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x24, 0xFCE8    ;                                 (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x26, 0xC401    ; stmia r4!, {r0}
    expect16_at 0x28, 0x9803    ; ldr   r0, [sp, #0xC]
    expect16_at 0x2A, 0x1CB6    ; add   r6, r6, #2
    expect16_at 0x2C, 0x1838    ; add   r0, r7, r0
    expect16_at 0x2E, 0x309C    ; add   r0, #0x9C
    expect16_at 0x30, 0x6800    ; ldr   r0, [r0]                damage
    expect16_at 0x32, 0x8028    ; strh  r0, [r5]
    expect16_at 0x34, 0x9802    ; ldr   r0, [sp, #8]
    expect16_at 0x36, 0x1CAD    ; add   r5, r5, #2
    expect16_at 0x38, 0x1C41    ; add   r1, r0, #1
    expect16_at 0x3A, 0x9801    ; ldr   r0, [sp, #4]
    expect16_at 0x3C, 0x9102    ; str   r1, [sp, #8]
    expect16_at 0x3E, 0x4281    ; cmp   r1, r0
    expect16_at 0x40, 0xDBE6    ; blt   loop

    ; The hit sound, by the effectiveness class args[1] (r2 = args, untouched since the entry).
    ldr     r0, [r2, #4]                    ; class: 1 normal, 2 super effective, 3 not very effective
    sub     r1, r0, #1
    cmp     r1, #2
    bhi     @@lists                         ; any other class: no sound
    cmp     r0, #1
    bne     @@play
    mov     r0, #4                          ; normal -> KOUKA_M
@@play:
    mov     r1, #(SEQ_SE_DP_KOUKA_BASE / 8)
    lsl     r1, r1, #3
    add     r0, r0, r1
    add     r0, #(SEQ_SE_DP_KOUKA_BASE - (SEQ_SE_DP_KOUKA_BASE / 8) * 8)
    bl      PlaySE                          ; 1788 / 1789 / 1790

    ; The target and damage lists, as before: object of each battler id, damage, count targets.
@@lists:
    add     r6, r7, #0
    add     r6, #0x98                       ; r6 = &BattleClient+0x98 (battler id), +4 damage; 8 per target
    add     r4, sp, #0x18                   ; objects
    add     r5, sp, #0x10                   ; damages (u16)
    ldr     r0, [sp, #4]
    str     r0, [sp, #8]                    ; remaining = count
@@loop:
    ldr     r0, [sp, #8]
    sub     r0, #1
    bmi     BattleAct_MoveDamage_Start
    str     r0, [sp, #8]
    ldrh    r0, [r6, #4]
    strh    r0, [r5]
    add     r5, #2
    ldrb    r1, [r6]
    add     r6, #8
    ldr     r0, [r7, #0x28]
    bl      BattleClient_GetMonObject
    stmia   r4!, {r0}
    b       @@loop
.endarea
.if org() != BattleAct_MoveDamage_Start
    .error "battle-hit-sound: the rewritten step 0 must end at 0x02204D50"
.endif

.close
```

## battle-message-error-marker

**Battle text: the hack's error marker before a Pokémon name prints '(Error) ' instead of Chinese (错误)**

- Kind: code
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Required by: `type-change-message`
- Decisions: D-2284
- Source: `work/patches/battle-message-error-marker/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: some battle messages show two Chinese characters in parentheses, (错误) ('error'), in front of a
Pokémon's name. Reported for rc6: 'the foe (2 Chinese characters) Pikachu's accuracy...' in a battle with
Camper Ward's Nuzleaf on Route 24 (Nature Power), and 'an untranslated Chinese word after
attract/infatuation' (the message printed each turn while the foe is infatuated). The untouched Chinese ROM
prints the same marker in the same places, so it is the hack's, not a missing translation; it is not in any
message bank, so the text translation could not reach it.

Status: D-1337 says hack bugs are reported, not fixed. This fix is a user-approved exception to it
(D-2284, 2026-10-09). It changes only the marker's text; why it appears and which name follows it are the
hack's logic and stay as they are (D-2285, open).

Technical: the battle message formatter in overlay 14 (0x02225A3C) expands a battle_string template control
code by control code. For the Pokémon-name tags (0x0101, 0x0102) it calls a helper (0x02225978 / 0x022259C4)
with the message's Pokémon reference; for a reference outside 1..25 (or one that resolves to nothing) the
helper buffers reference 1 instead and returns 0, and the formatter then appends four hardcoded character
codes to the output, '(' 错 误 ')', each with 'ldr r1, =char; add r0, r5, #0; bl String_AddChar'
(0x02225B16 for tag 0x0101, 0x02225B4A for 0x0102, codes in the literal pool at 0x02225C10), before the
name buffer. The ROM-wide hardcoded-text scan looks for 0xFFFF-terminated strings, so it could not see four
separate immediates. A sweep of every String_AddChar call in arm9 and all overlays finds no other Chinese
character (work/notes/battle-text-chinese_fix.md 'Sweep').

**What (old → new):**

Old: '(' 错 误 ')' appended before the name (four AddChar calls, 34 bytes per tag case); the fix writes 34 + 20 bytes.

New: the tag 0x0101 case's 34 bytes become a loop that appends a 0xFFFF-terminated string with
String_AddChar (r4, the tag's buffer index, saved and restored around it; r5, the output, unchanged) and
ends with the same branch to the formatter's common tail (0x02225BBA); the 0x0102 case's first halfword
branches to that loop and its next 18 bytes hold the string '(Error) ' (8 characters; the space separates
it from the name); the rest of that old path (12 bytes, dead after the branch) is left alone. Same conditions, same name after it, same tail: only the text differs. The literal pool
stays (no longer read). Not changed: the helpers, the fallback to reference 1, the message ids, the variant
(own / wild / foe) choice.

**Evidence:**

- D-2284: the user-approved exception to D-1337 for this fix; D-2285: the hack logic that makes the marker appear (open, not changed)
- work/notes/battle-text-chinese_fix.md: the formatter, the two cases, the sweep, the emulator runs before and after
- Runtime: emu_harness.py fixes --case battle-message-error-marker (scenario battle-error-marker: Camper Ward on Route 24 with the battle's first Pokémon-name buffer forced to an invalid reference, since battle-message-references fixed the hack's own sources; the characters the formatter's error path appends are hooked at String_AddChar). 2026-10-09, DeSmuME: the Chinese ROM and the --without build append ( 错 误 ), the full build '(Error) ' ('Ward sent out (Error) Linoone!'). Before battle-message-references, Nature Power reached it unforced: '(错误)直冲熊的命中率巨幅提高了！' (Chinese ROM), '(Error) Linoone’s accuracy rose drastically!' (build)
- melonDS 1.1 (headless backend), 2026-10-09: a wild battle on Route 24 grass, Linoone with Nature Power: '(错误)Maximilian’s accuracy rose drastically!' on the --without build, '(Error) Maximilian’s accuracy rose drastically!' on the full build; the battle goes on, no ARM9 abort or undefined instruction on either (work/notes/battle-text-chinese_fix.md)

**Touches:**

- `overlay14+0x25336` (RAM 0x02225B16) `battle-message-error-marker-tag0101`: 34 bytes, was `493E 1C28 F601 FA5F … (17 halfwords)`
- `overlay14+0x2536A` (RAM 0x02225B4A) `battle-message-error-marker-tag0102`: 20 bytes, was `4931 1C28 F601 FA45 … (10 halfwords)`

**Disassembly snapshot:** [`battle-message-error-marker.listing`](battle-message-error-marker/battle-message-error-marker.listing) (every edit, old → new; `python3 work/tools/asmpatch.py listing --write battle-message-error-marker`)

**Source** (`work/patches/battle-message-error-marker/battle-message-error-marker.asm`, armips; the new bytes):

<details>
<summary>battle-message-error-marker.asm</summary>

```asm
; battle-message-error-marker - the battle text's error marker (错误) reads "(Error) " in English. D-2284
; (user-approved exception to D-1337; the logic that makes it appear is the hack's, D-2285).
; Why and what: fix.toml next to this file; overview work/patches/FIXES.md;
; work/notes/battle-text-chinese_fix.md.
;
; The hack's battle message formatter (overlay 14, BattleMsg_Format 0x02225A3C) expands a battle_string
; template into the output String (r5) one control code at a time. For the Pokemon-name tags (0x0101 and
; 0x0102, jump-table cases 1 and 2) it calls a helper with the message's Pokemon reference
; (BattleMsg_BufferMonName1 0x02225978 / BattleMsg_BufferMonName2 0x022259C4). The helper accepts references
; 1..25; for 0 or > 25, or one that resolves to nothing, it buffers reference 1 instead and returns 0. On a 0
; the formatter appends four hardcoded characters to the output, '(' 错 误 ')' ("(error)") through
; String_AddChar (arm9 0x02026FDC), one 'ldr r1, =char; add r0, r5, #0; bl String_AddChar' per character, the
; codes in a shared literal pool (0x02225C10-0x02225C1C), and then goes on to the common tail (0x02225BBA),
; which appends the name buffer. So the marker prints in front of a name, the name being what the fallback
; buffered (observed: the player's first party Pokemon, also while another one is fighting). It is the only
; Chinese the battle prints outside battle_string.narc (work/notes/battle-text-chinese_fix.md 'Sweep').
;
; The fix keeps the logic (when the marker prints, and which name follows it, are the hack's) and only
; changes the text: case 1's 34 bytes become a loop that appends a 0xFFFF-terminated English string, and
; case 2's first instruction branches to it; the English sits in the next 18 bytes of case 2. r4 (the tag's
; buffer index, read again at the tail) is saved around the loop; r5 (the output) is not changed. The loop
; ends with the same branch to the tail as before. The literal pool is left as it is (no longer read).

.nds
.thumb
.include "../include/guards.inc"
.include "../include/charmap.inc"

.definelabel BattleMsg_Format,          0x02225A3C   ; (fmt, params, String *out, template) - not changed
.definelabel BattleMsg_BufferMonName1,  0x02225978   ; tag case 1 helper: 0 = bad reference
.definelabel BattleMsg_BufferMonName2,  0x022259C4   ; tag case 2 helper: 0 = bad reference
.definelabel BattleMsg_Case1,           0x02225B04   ; jump-table case 1 (tag 0x0101)
.definelabel BattleMsg_Case1Error,      0x02225B16   ; four AddChar calls: ( 错 误 )   <- rewritten
.definelabel BattleMsg_Case2,           0x02225B38   ; jump-table case 2 (tag 0x0102)
.definelabel BattleMsg_Case2Error,      0x02225B4A   ; four AddChar calls: ( 错 误 )   <- rewritten
.definelabel BattleMsg_TagDone,         0x02225BBA   ; common tail: append the tag's buffer (r4) to r5
.definelabel BattleMsg_ErrorPool,       0x02225C10   ; literal pool: 0x1B9 0xCED 0xBDD 0x1BA
.definelabel String_AddChar,            0x02026FDC   ; arm9: (String *, u16 char)

.open "overlay14.bin", 0x022007E0

; Read-only guards: the two cases up to their error branches and the literal pool.
.org BattleMsg_Case1
    expect16_at 0x00, 0x00A0    ; lsl   r0, r4, #2
    expect16_at 0x02, 0x5838    ; ldr   r0, [r7, r0]            params[r4]: the Pokemon reference
    expect16_at 0x04, 0x1C21    ; add   r1, r4, #0
    expect16_at 0x06, 0x0600    ; lsl   r0, r0, #0x18
    expect16_at 0x08, 0x0E00    ; lsr   r0, r0, #0x18
    expect16_at 0x0A, 0xF7FF    ; bl    BattleMsg_BufferMonName1 (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x0C, 0xFF33    ;                                (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x0E, 0x2800    ; cmp   r0, #0
    expect16_at 0x10, 0xD151    ; bne   BattleMsg_TagDone       name buffered: no marker
.org BattleMsg_Case2
    expect16_at 0x00, 0x00A0    ; lsl   r0, r4, #2
    expect16_at 0x02, 0x5838    ; ldr   r0, [r7, r0]
    expect16_at 0x04, 0x1C21    ; add   r1, r4, #0
    expect16_at 0x06, 0x0600    ; lsl   r0, r0, #0x18
    expect16_at 0x08, 0x0E00    ; lsr   r0, r0, #0x18
    expect16_at 0x0A, 0xF7FF    ; bl    BattleMsg_BufferMonName2 (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x0C, 0xFF3F    ;                                (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x0E, 0x2800    ; cmp   r0, #0
    expect16_at 0x10, 0xD137    ; bne   BattleMsg_TagDone
.org BattleMsg_ErrorPool
    expect32_at 0x0, 0x000001B9 ; (
    expect32_at 0x4, 0x00000CED ; 错
    expect32_at 0x8, 0x00000BDD ; 误
    expect32_at 0xC, 0x000001BA ; )

; Case 1's error path: a loop over ErrorMarker_Text.
.org BattleMsg_Case1Error
.area 0x22
    expect16_at 0x00, 0x493E    ; ldr   r1, =0x1B9              (
    expect16_at 0x02, 0x1C28    ; add   r0, r5, #0
    expect16_at 0x04, 0xF601    ; bl    String_AddChar          (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x06, 0xFA5F    ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x08, 0x493D    ; ldr   r1, =0xCED              错
    expect16_at 0x0A, 0x1C28
    expect16_at 0x0C, 0xF601
    expect16_at 0x0E, 0xFA5B
    expect16_at 0x10, 0x493C    ; ldr   r1, =0xBDD              误
    expect16_at 0x12, 0x1C28
    expect16_at 0x14, 0xF601
    expect16_at 0x16, 0xFA57
    expect16_at 0x18, 0x493B    ; ldr   r1, =0x1BA              )
    expect16_at 0x1A, 0x1C28
    expect16_at 0x1C, 0xF601
    expect16_at 0x1E, 0xFA53
    expect16_at 0x20, 0xE040    ; b     BattleMsg_TagDone
ErrorMarker:
    push    r4                              ; r4 = the tag's buffer index, read again at BattleMsg_TagDone
    add     r4, pc, ErrorMarker_Text - ((. + 4) & ~3)
@@next:
    ldrh    r1, [r4]
    add     r0, r1, #1
    lsr     r0, r0, #16                     ; 1 only for the 0xFFFF end
    bne     @@end
    add     r0, r5, #0                      ; the output String
    bl      String_AddChar
    add     r4, #2
    b       @@next
@@end:
    pop     r4
    b       BattleMsg_TagDone
    .fill BattleMsg_Case1Error + 0x22 - ., 0x00   ; unused (never reached)
.endarea

; Case 2's error path: the same loop. The English follows the branch, in the bytes up to 0x02225B5E; the
; rest of case 2's old error path (0x02225B5E-0x02225B6B, now dead) is left as it is, so the type-name case of
; the type-change-message fix can live there.
.org BattleMsg_Case2Error
.area 0x14
    expect16_at 0x00, 0x4931    ; ldr   r1, =0x1B9              (
    expect16_at 0x02, 0x1C28    ; add   r0, r5, #0
    expect16_at 0x04, 0xF601    ; bl    String_AddChar          (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x06, 0xFA45    ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x08, 0x4930    ; ldr   r1, =0xCED              错
    expect16_at 0x0A, 0x1C28
    expect16_at 0x0C, 0xF601
    expect16_at 0x0E, 0xFA41
    expect16_at 0x10, 0x492F    ; ldr   r1, =0xBDD              误
    expect16_at 0x12, 0x1C28
    b       ErrorMarker
    .align 4, 0x00
ErrorMarker_Text:
    ; "(Error) ": 错误 = error; the space separates it from the name after it. 0xFFFF ends it.
    .halfword CH_LPAREN, CH_E, CH_LC_R, CH_LC_R, CH_LC_O, CH_LC_R, CH_RPAREN, CH_SPACE, 0xFFFF
.endarea

.close
```

## battle-message-references

**Battle text: Nature Power's 'turned into' line and the per-turn infatuation line name the right Pokémon**

- Kind: code
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-2286
- Source: `work/patches/battle-message-references/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: after Nature Power the game said "(Error) <your first party Pokémon>'s accuracy rose drastically!" (in
Chinese '(错误)…的命中率巨幅提高了！') instead of "Nature Power turned into <move>!", even when the foe used it and
the named Pokémon was benched (rc6 report: "the foe (2 Chinese characters) Pikachu's accuracy…" against Camper
Ward's Nuzleaf on Route 24). Every turn an infatuated Pokémon tried to move, the game said "The foe's (Error)
<your Pokémon> fell in love with <the infatuated foe>!": the names in the wrong places and one of them the
fallback (rc6 report: "an untranslated Chinese word after attract/infatuation"). The untouched Chinese ROM does
the same (D-2285).

Status: D-1337 says hack bugs are reported, not fixed. This fix is a user-approved exception to it (D-2286,
2026-10-09, resolves D-2285). The error marker itself is translated by battle-message-error-marker (D-2284) and
stays as a safety net.

Technical: the hack builds battle messages as records (MsgRec_Init 0x02225DC0: type, id; MsgRec_AddArg
0x02225DEC). Type 1 prints battle_string bank 2, type 2 bank 1 (own / wild / foe / trainer variants); the
arguments are the template's buffers, and a Pokémon-name buffer needs a Pokémon reference 1..25 (1-6 the player's
party, 13-18 the foe's). Nature Power (0x0223F070) builds MsgRec_Init(rec, 2, 120) with one argument, the called
move (battle var 0x29): message 120 with a move is bank 2's 'Nature Power turned into {move}!', but type 2
printed bank 1's #120 with the move id as the Pokémon (Earthquake = 89 > 25). The infatuation check before a
Pokémon moves (0x0221DAEC) emits 1#452 ({0} = the infatuated Pokémon, which also picks the variant; {1} = the one
it is in love with) with the arguments (condition 7's data field, self): the data field (0x02216D4C) is always 0
for infatuation (observed), the attracter is the condition's source (word 0 of its entry, Pokémon + 0x70:
observed 0x0D for a wild attracter, 0x01 for the player's), and the order is reversed.

**What (old → new):**

Old: Nature Power -> record type 2, id 120 -> 1#120-123 with the move as the Pokémon; infatuation -> 1#452 with
(0, self).

New: 0x0223F084 'movs r1, #2' -> 'movs r1, #1' (type 1: 2#120 'Nature Power turned into {move}!', the move
argument unchanged). 0x0221DAFC: the call reading the condition's data field (and its byte mask) becomes 'ldr
r4, [r5, #0x70]' with the same byte mask (the condition's source) and a nop; 0x0221DB20: the two argument stores
are swapped, so the arguments are (self, source). Not changed: the message ids, the variant battler, when the
messages appear, the condition logic. A static audit of every message record and stream message in overlay 14
(284 records, 103 direct emits) found no other argument that can be a non-reference in a Pokémon-name slot
(work/notes/battle-text-chinese_fix.md 'Audit').

**Evidence:**

- D-2286: the user-approved exception to D-1337 for this fix; it resolves the hack finding D-2285
- work/notes/battle-text-chinese_fix.md: the record types, the two call sites, the audit, the emulator runs before and after
- Runtime: emu_harness.py fixes --case battle-message-references (scenario battle-references: Linoone with only Nature Power against Camper Ward on Route 24, then a wild Chansey with only Attract against a Tauros; the message records and the battle_string ids the client reads). 2026-10-09, DeSmuME: the Chinese ROM and the --without build read 1#120 and 1#452 with an invalid reference; the full build reads 2#120 and 1#452 with (self, attracter)

**Touches:**

- `overlay14+0x3E8A4` (RAM 0x0223F084) `battle-message-references-nature-power`: 2 bytes, was `2102`
- `overlay14+0x1D31C` (RAM 0x0221DAFC) `battle-message-references-infatuation-source`: 8 bytes, was `F7F9 F926 0600 0E04`
- `overlay14+0x1D340` (RAM 0x0221DB20) `battle-message-references-infatuation-args`: 4 bytes, was `9400 9001`

**Disassembly snapshot:** [`battle-message-references.listing`](battle-message-references/battle-message-references.listing) (every edit, old → new; `python3 work/tools/asmpatch.py listing --write battle-message-references`)

**Source** (`work/patches/battle-message-references/battle-message-references.asm`, armips; the new bytes):

<details>
<summary>battle-message-references.asm</summary>

```asm
; battle-message-references - battle messages that named the wrong Pokemon (or printed the error marker):
; Nature Power's 'turned into' line and the per-turn infatuation line. D-2286 (user-approved exception to D-1337;
; resolves the hack finding D-2285).
; Why and what: fix.toml next to this file; overview work/patches/FIXES.md; work/notes/battle-text-chinese_fix.md.
;
; The hack builds most battle messages as a message record (MsgRec_Init 0x02225DC0: record, type, message id;
; MsgRec_AddArg 0x02225DEC: one argument). Type 1 prints battle_string bank 2 (plain lines, the arguments are the
; template's buffers); type 2 prints bank 1 (own / wild / foe / trainer variants, chosen from a battler, the
; arguments again the buffers). A Pokemon-name buffer (tags 0x0101 / 0x0102) needs a Pokemon reference 1..25
; (1-6 the player's party, 13-18 the foe's, ...); anything else prints the error marker (see
; battle-message-error-marker) and the name of reference 1, the player's first party Pokemon.
;
; 1. Nature Power (NaturePower_ShowCalledMove 0x0223F070): the record is MsgRec_Init(rec, 2, 120) plus the called
;    move (battle var 0x29). Message 120 with one move argument is bank 2's 'Nature Power turned into {move}!'
;    (2#120); type 2 printed bank 1's 120, '{Pokemon}'s accuracy rose drastically!', with the move id as the
;    Pokemon reference (Earthquake 89 on Route 24). The fix: type 1.
; 2. Infatuation, every turn the infatuated Pokemon tries to move (Turn_CheckInfatuation 0x0221DAEC): it emits
;    1#452 '{1}让{0}着迷了' / 'The foe's {0} fell in love with {1}!' with the arguments (condition 7's data,
;    self). Condition 7's data field (0x02216D4C) is always 0 for infatuation; the Pokemon it is in love with is
;    the condition's source, word 0 of its 8-byte entry (Pokemon + 0x38 + 7 * 8 = + 0x70: observed 0x0D for a wild
;    attracter, 0x01 for the player's). And {0} is the infatuated Pokemon (the variant is chosen from it), {1}
;    the attracter, so the two arguments were also swapped. The fix: r4 = the source's low byte, then
;    (self, source).

.nds
.thumb
.include "../include/guards.inc"

.definelabel NaturePower_ShowCalledMove,  0x0223F070   ; battle event: Nature Power picked its move
.definelabel NaturePower_RecordType,      0x0223F084   ; movs r1, #2 (record type)  <- 1
.definelabel Turn_CheckInfatuation,       0x0221DAEC   ; condition 7 (infatuation) before the Pokemon moves
.definelabel Infatuation_ReadData,        0x0221DAFC   ; bl Condition_GetData(mon, 7)  <- ldr the source
.definelabel Infatuation_StoreArgs,       0x0221DB20   ; str r4, [sp] / str r0, [sp, #4]  <- swapped
.definelabel Condition_GetData,           0x02216D4C   ; (mon, condition) -> the entry's data field
.definelabel Mon_GetRef,                  0x022167A0   ; mon -> its Pokemon reference ([mon + 0x14])
.definelabel MsgRec_Init,                 0x02225DC0
.definelabel MsgRec_AddArg,               0x02225DEC
.definelabel BattleMsg_Emit,              0x02224C50   ; (stream, op, id, variant battler, args..., 0xFFFF)
.definelabel BattleVar_Get,               0x0220FCC0

.open "overlay14.bin", 0x022007E0

; 1. Nature Power: read-only guard of the routine, then the record type.
.org NaturePower_ShowCalledMove
    expect16_at 0x00, 0xB510    ; push  {r4, lr}
    expect16_at 0x02, 0x2006    ; movs  r0, #6
    expect16_at 0x04, 0x1C0C    ; adds  r4, r1, #0
    expect16_at 0x06, 0xF7D0    ; bl    BattleVar_Get           (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x08, 0xFE23    ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x0A, 0x4284    ; cmp   r4, r0
    expect16_at 0x0C, 0xD112    ; bne   (not this battler's move)
    expect16_at 0x0E, 0x2003    ; movs  r0, #3
    expect16_at 0x10, 0xF7D0    ; bl    BattleVar_Get           (1/2)  var 3: the message record
    expect16_at 0x12, 0xFE1E    ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x16, 0x2278    ; movs  r2, #0x78               message 120
    expect16_at 0x18, 0x1C04    ; adds  r4, r0, #0
    expect16_at 0x1A, 0xF7E6    ; bl    MsgRec_Init             (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x1C, 0xFE99    ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x1E, 0x2029    ; movs  r0, #0x29               var 0x29: the called move
    expect16_at 0x20, 0xF7D0    ; bl    BattleVar_Get           (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x22, 0xFE16    ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x24, 0x1C01    ; adds  r1, r0, #0
    expect16_at 0x26, 0x1C20    ; adds  r0, r4, #0
    expect16_at 0x28, 0xF7E6    ; bl    MsgRec_AddArg           (1/2)  the only argument
    expect16_at 0x2A, 0xFEA8    ;                               (2/2)

.org NaturePower_RecordType
.area 2
    expect16 0x2102             ; movs  r1, #2                  type 2: bank 1, variants
    mov     r1, #1              ; type 1: bank 2, 'Nature Power turned into {move}!'
.endarea

; 2. Infatuation: read-only guard of the message's emit, then the two edits.
.org Turn_CheckInfatuation
    expect16_at 0x00, 0x1C28    ; adds  r0, r5, #0              r5 = the Pokemon about to move
    expect16_at 0x02, 0x2107    ; movs  r1, #7
    expect16_at 0x04, 0xF7F9    ; bl    (has condition 7?)      (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x06, 0xF91A    ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x08, 0x2800    ; cmp   r0, #0
    expect16_at 0x0A, 0xD026    ; beq   (not infatuated)
    expect16_at 0x18, 0x1C28    ; adds  r0, r5, #0
    expect16_at 0x1A, 0x2107    ; movs  r1, #7
    expect16_at 0x1C, 0xF00C    ; bl    0x0222A434              (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x1E, 0xFC94    ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x26, 0x1C28    ; adds  r0, r5, #0
    expect16_at 0x28, 0xF7F8    ; bl    Mon_GetRef              (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x2A, 0xFE44    ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x2C, 0x1C07    ; adds  r7, r0, #0              r7 = variant battler: self
    expect16_at 0x2E, 0x1C28    ; adds  r0, r5, #0
    expect16_at 0x30, 0xF7F8    ; bl    Mon_GetRef              (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x32, 0xFE40    ;                               (2/2)  r0 = self
    expect16_at 0x3A, 0x2271    ; movs  r2, #0x71               (<< 2 = 452)
    expect16_at 0x40, 0x2103    ; movs  r1, #3                  op 3: bank 1, variants
    expect16_at 0x42, 0x0092    ; lsls  r2, r2, #2
    expect16_at 0x44, 0x1C3B    ; adds  r3, r7, #0
    expect16_at 0x46, 0xF007    ; bl    BattleMsg_Emit          (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x48, 0xF88D    ;                               (2/2)

.org Infatuation_ReadData
.area 8
    expect16_at 0, 0xF7F9       ; bl    Condition_GetData       (1/2)  the data field: 0
    expect16_at 2, 0xF926       ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 4, 0x0600       ; lsls  r0, r0, #0x18
    expect16_at 6, 0x0E04       ; lsrs  r4, r0, #0x18
    ldr     r4, [r5, #0x70]     ; condition 7's source: the Pokemon it is in love with
    lsl     r4, r4, #0x18
    lsr     r4, r4, #0x18
    mov     r8, r8              ; nop
.endarea

.org Infatuation_StoreArgs
.area 4
    expect16_at 0, 0x9400       ; str   r4, [sp]                {0} = the attracter
    expect16_at 2, 0x9001       ; str   r0, [sp, #4]            {1} = self
    str     r0, [sp]            ; {0}: self, the infatuated Pokemon
    str     r4, [sp, #4]        ; {1}: the Pokemon it is in love with
.endarea

.close
```

</details>

## battle-message-variant

**Battle text: 'The wild' / 'The foe's' goes with the Pokémon the line names (Destiny Knot, Mean Look, Protect, drain, immunity, ...)**

- Kind: code
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-2319
- Source: `work/patches/battle-message-variant/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: when one Pokémon's move, Ability or held item affects another Pokémon, the battle line about the
affected Pokémon could lose or gain its 'The wild' / 'The foe's' prefix, because the game took the prefix
from the Pokémon that caused it. A wild Chansey's Attract on a Tauros holding a Destiny Knot printed
'Chansey fell in love because of the Destiny Knot!' (the wild Chansey, without 'The wild'); the other way
round, the player's own Pokémon was called 'The wild ...'. In a trainer battle the player's Pokémon is called
'The foe's ...'. The same happened to Mean Look and Block ('can no longer escape'), Curse, Poison Point,
Gastro Acid, Smack Down, Octolock and the other condition lines listed below, to four 'HP was restored'
handlers and to Heal Block's 'can't heal'; and to move lines about the target: 'The wild Rattata protected
itself' printed as 'Rattata protected itself', likewise 'had its energy drained', 'It doesn't seem to affect
...', 'It had no effect at all on ...', 'is already poisoned' (and the other 'already ...' lines), 'couldn't
stay airborne because of gravity', 'anchored itself with its roots' and the Pledge 'is waiting for ...'.
The untouched Chinese ROM does the same (it drops or adds 野生的 / 对手的), so this is a bug of the hack.

Status: D-1337 says hack bugs are reported, not fixed. This fix is a user-approved exception to it
(D-2319, 2026-10-09: 'Please fix'; the move lines in round 2: 'Yes, same branch'); other hack bugs stay
report-only.

Technical: bank 1 of battle_string has four forms of each line (the player's, wild, foe's, a trainer's); the
server sends a line with a 'variant battler' and the client picks the form from that battler's side
(0x02225E40). The form belongs to the Pokémon the prefix stands before.
1. The condition applier (overlay 14, 0x0221E53C, called through 0x0221F87C and its queued path 0x0221E05C)
   sends a message record its caller built with the source's battler when there is a source (0x0221E548:
   cmp r0, #0; beq), else the target's; its own default message uses the target. Every caller whose record
   names a Pokémon in the prefixed slot and whose source and target differ names the target (static audit of
   all 51 calls, work/notes/destiny-knot-side_fix.md): Destiny Knot 1#448 (0x0220AECC: source = the holder),
   item-inflicted conditions through 0x0220C838, Poison Point-type poisoning 1#638, 1#324, Mean Look / Block /
   other trapping 1#1180 (three handlers), Curse 1#1442 ({1} = the cursed one = the target), 1#754, Gastro
   Acid-type 1#762 and 1#1836, 1#1840, Smack Down 1#1530, Electrify 1#1604, Powder 1#1624, Octolock 1#1958.
2. The change applier 0x0221F968 sends its record with the source's battler (0x0221FA1C: ldrb r1, [r4]).
   Four callers name the target there (1#524 'HP was restored', 0x0223A9DC, 0x0223DEBC, 0x02244598,
   0x02246430); two name the source (1#944 Wish, 1#2138); the rest have source = target.
3. In the same function Heal Block's 1#1200 '{0} can't heal' is sent with the source's battler and the
   target as {0} (0x0221FA4A).
4. Move code that sends its line itself (stream op 3 via 0x02229E1C / 0x02224C50, or the condition check's
   'already ...' helper 0x02229944) passes the attacker's or move user's battler while the line names the
   target: 1#296 (0x0221A7B8), 1#288 (0x0221AE92, 0x0221AEB6, 0x0221AF34, 0x0221B228, 0x0221B8F6), Protect
   1#706 (0x0221B384), drain 1#1220 (0x0221C1FC), the condition check 0x0221E0AC (struct source instead of
   target, 0x0221E0E8: 1#340 and the other lines of 0x02229944), Gravity 1#1468 (0x0220E4DA), Ingrain 1#1000
   (0x02220B78); Pledge 1#1554 (0x02222DE2) puts the prefix on {1} but passes {0}'s battler.

**What (old → new):**

Old: 1. variant = source, else target; 2. variant = source; 3. variant = source.

New: 1. variant = target, else source (0x0221E548, 10 bytes: cmp r5, #0; bne -> the old target path;
cmp r0, #0; beq -> no variant; b -> the old call with r0 = source; the old source path's last four
instructions are no longer reached). 2. variant = the record's first parameter (0x0221FA1C, 6 bytes: the
record address first, then ldrb r1, [r0, #4]). 3. variant = target (0x0221FA4A, 2 bytes: ldrb r0, [r4, #1]).
4. One halfword per site (24 bytes): the variant is the register or field that already holds the named
Pokémon (the target, or {0} / {1}); the attacker's value is still computed and no longer used.
Not changed: message ids and parameters, which Pokémon gets the condition and the stored source (the
infatuation message still names the attracter), the default messages, and every line whose variant already
was the Pokémon it names: the new choice equals the old one whenever source and target (1, 3) or source and
first parameter (2) are the same Pokémon, or (4) attacker and target are. Not covered (reported in
work/notes/destiny-knot-side_fix.md): Lock-On / Mind Reader 1#878 (prefix on {1} while the condition and its
message belong to the user: needs new code, no room in place) and 1#1410 (0x02221F56, variant from a stack
argument whose source was not found; not confirmed).

**Evidence:**

- D-2319: the user-approved exception to D-1337 for this fix (user, 2026-10-09: 'Please fix', round 2 'Yes, same branch'; found by the reviewer of fix/battle-text-chinese)
- work/notes/destiny-knot-side_fix.md: the message path, the static audit of every condition-applier and change-applier call and of the move-line sites, the runtime checks
- Runtime: emu_harness.py fixes --case battle-message-variant (scenario battle-variant: ten wild battles, Destiny Knot both ways, Mean Look, Protect, Giga Drain, Tackle on a Ghost, Toxic again, Horn Drill on a higher level, Roar after Ingrain, Gravity during Fly; the client's bank-1 printer 0x02225EA8 hooked: variant battler against {0}). 2026-10-09, DeSmuME, PASS: the full build has variant = {0} in all ten, the --without build and the untouched Chinese ROM the other Pokémon in all ten
- DeSmuME 2026-10-09, more battles (work/notes/destiny-knot-side_fix.md): Mean Look against Camper Ward's Nuzleaf ('The foe's Nuzleaf can no longer escape!'), Curse (prefix on {1}): original on the control and the Chinese ROM, fixed on the full build; Lock-On 1#878 unchanged (not covered); battle sweep 24/24
- melonDS 1.1 (headless backend), 2026-10-09, Route 24 grass against a wild Shroomish: Mean Look 'The wild Shroomish can no longer escape!' and Toxic again 'The wild Shroomish is already poisoned.' on the full build, 'Shroomish ...' on the --without build; no ARM9 abort, prefetch abort or undefined instruction, no hang (work/notes/destiny-knot-side_fix.md)

<details>
<summary>battle-message-variant.asm</summary>

```asm
; battle-message-variant - battle lines that one Pokemon's effect prints about another Pokemon pick their
; own / wild / foe's / trainer's form from the Pokemon they name (Destiny Knot: "The wild Chansey fell in love
; because of the Destiny Knot!"). D-2319 (user-approved exception to D-1337).
; Why and what: fix.toml next to this file; overview work/patches/FIXES.md; work/notes/destiny-knot-side_fix.md.
;
; Bank 1 of battle_string has four forms of each line: plain (the player's Pokemon), 'The wild ...', 'The
; foe's ...' and '<trainer>'s ...'. The server sends the line with a variant battler (stream op 3); the client
; picks the form from that battler's side (0x02225E40) and fills the template's parameters. The form belongs to
; the Pokemon the prefix stands before, so the variant battler has to be that Pokemon.
;
; 1. Condition applier (0x0221E53C; reached from ApplyCondition 0x0221F87C and its queued path 0x0221E05C).
;    Its struct holds the source (the Pokemon whose move, Ability or item causes it, [0]) and the target (the
;    one that gets the condition, [4]); a message record the caller built (+0x30 of its struct) is sent with
;    0x0222934C(record, variant). The variant is the source's when there is one, else the target's; its own
;    default message names the target and passes the target. Every caller with a record of its own whose source
;    and target differ names the target (static audit, work/notes/destiny-knot-side_fix.md), e.g. Destiny Knot
;    (0x0220AECC: source = the holder, target = the attacker, 1#448 "{target} fell in love because of the
;    {item}"), Mean Look / Block 1#1180, Curse 1#1442, Poison Point 1#638, Gastro Acid 1#762, Smack Down 1#1530,
;    Octolock 1#1958. Fix: test the target first (the source only when there is no target). 10 bytes.
; 2. Change applier (0x0221F968, ApplyHPChange with a message record at +0x20, source [0], target [1]): the
;    record is sent with the source's battler. Callers whose source differs from the record's first argument
;    name the target there (1#524 "{0}'s HP was restored", four handlers); two name the source (1#944, 1#2138).
;    Fix: the variant is the record's first argument (low byte of its first parameter, record + 4). 6 bytes.
; 3. Same function, Heal Block: 1#1200 "{0} can't heal because of Heal Block" is emitted with the source's
;    battler and the target as {0}. Fix: the target's battler. 2 bytes.
;
; Not changed: the message ids, the arguments, the default messages, which Pokemon gets the condition and its
; source, and every line whose variant already is the Pokemon it names (unchanged by construction: the new
; choice equals the old one whenever source and target, or source and first argument, are the same).

.nds
.thumb
.include "../include/guards.inc"

.definelabel CondApply_Message,         0x0221E53C   ; (src mon, tgt mon, cond, ...; default flag, record)
.definelabel CondApply_PickVariant,     0x0221E548   ; r1 = variant battler: src, else tgt   <- edit 1
.definelabel CondApply_VariantOfR5,     0x0221E55A   ; r0 = tgt; bl BattleMon_GetBattler; r1 = result
.definelabel CondApply_Ref,             0x0221E55C   ; bl BattleMon_GetBattler (r0 = a battle Pokemon)
.definelabel CondApply_VariantDone,     0x0221E564
.definelabel HPChange_SendRecord,       0x0221FA1C   ; 0x0222934C(record + 0x20, [struct]) <- edit 2
.definelabel HPChange_HealBlocked,      0x0221FA4A   ; 0x02229E1C([struct], 1200, [struct+1]) <- edit 3
.definelabel BattleMon_GetBattler,      0x022167A0   ; ldrb r0, [r0, #0x14]
.definelabel BattleMsg_SendRecord,      0x0222934C   ; (record, variant battler)
.definelabel BattleMsg_Emit1,           0x02229E1C   ; (variant battler, id, param)

.open "overlay14.bin", 0x022007E0

; Read-only guards: the applier's variant choice and both record sends (nothing is written here).
.org CondApply_Message
    expect16_at 0x00, 0xB40F    ; push  {r0, r1, r2, r3}
    expect16_at 0x02, 0xB530    ; push  {r4, r5, lr}
    expect16_at 0x04, 0xB089    ; sub   sp, #0x24
    expect16_at 0x06, 0x1C0D    ; adds  r5, r1, #0              r5 = target
    expect16_at 0x08, 0x1C14    ; adds  r4, r2, #0              r4 = condition
    expect16_at 0x0A, 0x2100    ; movs  r1, #0
    expect16_at 0x0C, 0x2800    ; cmp   r0, #0                  r0 = source  <- edit 1 (0x0C-0x15)
    expect16_at 0x0E, 0xD004    ; beq   0x0221E556
    expect16_at 0x10, 0xF7F8    ; bl    BattleMon_GetBattler    (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x12, 0xF928    ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x14, 0x0600    ; lsls  r0, r0, #0x18
    expect16_at 0x16, 0x0E01    ; lsrs  r1, r0, #0x18           variant = source
    expect16_at 0x18, 0xE006    ; b     CondApply_VariantDone
    expect16_at 0x1A, 0x2D00    ; cmp   r5, #0                  0x0221E556
    expect16_at 0x1C, 0xD004    ; beq   CondApply_VariantDone
    expect16_at 0x1E, 0x1C28    ; adds  r0, r5, #0              CondApply_VariantOfR5
    expect16_at 0x20, 0xF7F8    ; bl    BattleMon_GetBattler    (1/2)  CondApply_Ref
    expect16_at 0x22, 0xF920    ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x24, 0x0600    ; lsls  r0, r0, #0x18
    expect16_at 0x26, 0x0E01    ; lsrs  r1, r0, #0x18           variant = target
    expect16_at 0x28, 0x9811    ; ldr   r0, [sp, #0x44]         CondApply_VariantDone: default-message flag
    expect16_at 0x2A, 0x2800    ; cmp   r0, #0
    expect16_at 0x2C, 0xD032    ; beq   0x0221E5D0
    expect16_at 0x2E, 0x2D00    ; cmp   r5, #0
    expect16_at 0x30, 0xD030    ; beq   0x0221E5D0
    expect16_at 0x52, 0x1C28    ; adds  r0, r5, #0              default message: {0} = target
    expect16_at 0x54, 0xF7F8    ; bl    BattleMon_GetBattler    (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x56, 0xF906    ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x78, 0x1C28    ; adds  r0, r5, #0              ... and variant = target
    expect16_at 0x7A, 0xF7F8    ; bl    BattleMon_GetBattler    (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x7C, 0xF8F3    ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x7E, 0x1C01    ; adds  r1, r0, #0
    expect16_at 0x80, 0x0609    ; lsls  r1, r1, #0x18
    expect16_at 0x82, 0xA800    ; add   r0, sp, #0
    expect16_at 0x84, 0x0E09    ; lsrs  r1, r1, #0x18
    expect16_at 0x86, 0xF00A    ; bl    BattleMsg_SendRecord    (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x88, 0xFEC3    ;                               (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x94, 0x9812    ; ldr   r0, [sp, #0x48]         0x0221E5D0: the caller's record
    expect16_at 0x96, 0x2800    ; cmp   r0, #0
    expect16_at 0x98, 0xD001    ; beq   0x0221E5DA
    expect16_at 0x9A, 0xF00A    ; bl    BattleMsg_SendRecord    (1/2)  r1 = the variant chosen above
    expect16_at 0x9C, 0xFEB9    ;                               (2/2)

; Edit 1: the target's battler first, the source's only when there is no target. The old target branch

    cmp     r0, #0

    b       CondApply_Ref               ; only a source: its battler (r0 = source)
```

## battle-party-status-sync

**In-battle party screen: status conditions show as they are now (Heal Bell, Aromatherapy, statuses gained in battle)**

- Kind: code
- Enabled: yes
- Requires: nothing
- Decisions: D-2317
- Source: `work/patches/battle-party-status-sync/fix.toml`

**Why (the Chinese hack):**

Players: after Heal Bell or Aromatherapy cures the whole party, the Pokémon on the bench still show PSN, PAR,
BRN and so on in the party screen (a Discord report: 'just a visual bug': switched in, they are cured).
The same screen also never shows a status gained during the battle: a Pokémon burned by its Flame Orb shows
no BRN there. The untouched Chinese ROM does the same, so this is a bug of the hack.

Status: D-1337 says hack bugs are reported, not fixed. This fix is a user-approved exception to it
(D-2317, 2026-10-09); other hack bugs stay report-only.

Technical: the hack's battle engine (overlay 14) keeps a battle record per party member with its own status
table, and a pointer to the battle's copy of the party Pokémon at record+0x10. Status changes (inflicted,
cured by a move, item or ability, for the active Pokémon and the bench alike) change the record only; the
copy gets the record's status at the end of the battle, from BPP_ReflectToPP (0x02218B28: condition ->
party status bits, SetMonData status). The in-battle party screens are built from the copies: four loops
(0x022027DC, the POKéMON button; 0x02202B78, the Bag's 'use on which Pokémon'; 0x0220405C, the forced
switch after a faint; 0x02203DBC, 'Will you switch your Pokémon?' after the foe's Pokémon faints) add each member's copy to a new party. So these screens show the status from the start of the
battle. Switching in uses the record (the cured Pokémon has no status), and after the battle the party is
right.

**What (old → new):**

Old: party screen <- the battle's party copies, status as at the start of the battle.

New: ReflectToPP's status block (0x02218B52-0x02218BA1) is replaced by a call to a routine in the same
bytes, BPP_SyncSickToPP(record): the same conversion (fainted -> 0; PAR 0x40, SLP 2, FRZ 0x20, BRN 0x10,
PSN 0x08, as the hack's switch) and SetMonData status on the copy, returning the copy. ReflectToPP does
exactly what it did. The four party-screen loops call BPP_SyncSickToPP instead of BPP_GetSrcData
(0x022027E6, 0x02202B82, 0x02203DC6, 0x02204066: one bl each), so each copy carries its current status when
a party screen is built. Not changed: the cure and the status logic, the record, HP/PP/items/forms of the
copy, the end-of-battle copy (it writes the same status), the opponent's side, other screens that take one
Pokémon's copy (catching, 0x0222B99E; 0x0222F5B2).
The copy's status is set to what the end of the battle would write anyway, only earlier.

**Evidence:**

- D-2317: the user-approved exception to D-1337 for this fix (Discord report 'After using Heal Bell ... still displayed on the Pokémon in the swap screen'; user request 2026-10-09 to fix the reported bugs, one worktree each)
- work/notes/heal-bell-status_fix.md: the records, the copies, the four loops and the emulator runs before and after
- Reproduced 2026-10-09 (DeSmuME, trainer battle, lead Chansey with Heal Bell or Aromatherapy, bench PSN/PAR/BRN): the Chinese ROM and the build without this fix print the three cure messages (battle_string 1#336/380/360) and still show PSN/PAR/BRN in the party screen; the build with the fix shows none; Flame Orb's burn on the lead shows only with the fix
- Runtime: emu_harness.py fixes --case battle-party-status-sync (scenario healbell: Heal Bell in a trainer battle, then the POKéMON button; the status of every Pokémon the party screen draws; each run on the build and on one without this fix, work/notes/emu_harness.md 'Fix scenarios')

```asm
    expect16_at 0x12, 0x1800    ; adds  r0, r0, r0               switch (condition)

    expect16_at 0x1E, 0x0026    ; .hword: 0 none -> condition (0)
    expect16_at 0x20, 0x001C    ; .hword: 1 PAR  -> 0x40
    expect16_at 0x22, 0x0026    ; .hword: 2 SLP  -> condition (2)
    expect16_at 0x24, 0x0016    ; .hword: 3 FRZ  -> 0x20
    expect16_at 0x26, 0x0010    ; .hword: 4 BRN  -> 0x10
    expect16_at 0x28, 0x000A    ; .hword: 5 PSN  -> 0x08
    expect16_at 0x2A, 0x2008    ; movs  r0, #8
    expect16_at 0x2C, 0x9000    ; str   r0, [sp]
    expect16_at 0x2E, 0xE00A    ; b     store
    expect16_at 0x30, 0x2010    ; movs  r0, #0x10
    expect16_at 0x32, 0x9000    ; str   r0, [sp]
    expect16_at 0x34, 0xE007    ; b     store
    expect16_at 0x36, 0x2020    ; movs  r0, #0x20
    expect16_at 0x38, 0x9000    ; str   r0, [sp]
    expect16_at 0x3A, 0xE004    ; b     store
    expect16_at 0x3C, 0x2040    ; movs  r0, #0x40
    expect16_at 0x3E, 0x9000    ; str   r0, [sp]
    expect16_at 0x40, 0xE001    ; b     store
    expect16_at 0x42, 0x2000    ; movs  r0, #0                   fainted: no status
    expect16_at 0x44, 0x9000    ; str   r0, [sp]
    expect16_at 0x46, 0x6920    ; ldr   r0, [r4, #0x10]          store: the copy
    expect16_at 0x48, 0x21A0    ; movs  r1, #0xa0
    expect16_at 0x4A, 0xAA00    ; add   r2, sp, #0
    expect16_at 0x4C, 0xF655    ; bl    SetMonData (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x4E, 0xF9E7    ;                  (2/2)
    add     r0, r4, #0
    bl      BPP_SyncSickToPP
    b       ReflectToPP_Moves

; BPP_SyncSickToPP(r0 = bpp) -> r0 = the battle's party Pokemon (what BPP_GetSrcData returns), whose status
; is now the record's: the conversion ReflectToPP did inline (fainted -> 0; else SickToStatus). Keeps r4-r7.
BPP_SyncSickToPP:
    push    {r3, r4, r5, lr}
    add     r4, r0, #0
    bl      BPP_GetPokeSick         ; r0 = 0..5
    ldrh    r1, [r4, #0x1E]         ; current HP
    cmp     r1, #0
    beq     @@store                 ; fainted: status 0 (r1 = 0)
    add     r1, r15, #(SickToStatus - ((. + 4) & ~3))   ; adr r1, SickToStatus
    ldrb    r1, [r1, r0]
@@store:
    str     r1, [sp]                ; the pushed r3's slot
    ldr     r0, [r4, #0x10]         ; the battle's party Pokemon
    mov     r1, #0xA0               ; status
    add     r2, sp, #0
    bl      SetMonData
    ldr     r0, [r4, #0x10]
    pop     {r3, r4, r5, pc}
.align 4
SickToStatus:                       ; condition -> party status bits, as ReflectToPP's switch
    .byte   0x00                    ; 0 none
    .byte   0x40                    ; 1 PAR
    .byte   0x02                    ; 2 SLP (ReflectToPP stores the condition number, 2)
    .byte   0x20                    ; 3 FRZ
    .byte   0x10                    ; 4 BRN
    .byte   0x08                    ; 5 PSN
.align 2
    .fill   ReflectToPP_Moves - ., 0   ; the rest of the old block: no longer reached
.endarea

; Edits 2-5: the in-battle party screen loops take each member's party Pokemon through BPP_SyncSickToPP.
; Each loop: r0 = BtlParty_GetMember(party, i); bl <here>; add r1, r0, #0; ldr r0, [list]; bl Party_AddMon.
.macro party_list_src, addr, bl_hi, bl_lo, get_hi, get_lo, after
.org addr
    expect16_at -0x04, get_hi       ; bl    BtlParty_GetMember (1/2)
    expect16_at -0x02, get_lo       ;                          (2/2)
    expect16_at 0x04, 0x1C01        ; add   r1, r0, #0
    expect16_at 0x06, after         ; ldr   r0, [rN]          the new party
.area 4
    expect16_at 0x00, bl_hi         ; bl    BPP_GetSrcData (1/2)
    expect16_at 0x02, bl_lo         ;                      (2/2)
    bl      BPP_SyncSickToPP
.endarea
.endmacro

    party_list_src PartyList_Pokemon_Src, 0xF013, 0xFFE5, 0xF012, 0xFCDD, 0x6820
    party_list_src PartyList_2_Src,       0xF013, 0xFE17, 0xF012, 0xFB0F, 0x6830
    party_list_src PartyList_3_Src,       0xF012, 0xFCF5, 0xF011, 0xF9ED, 0x6838
    party_list_src PartyList_4_Src,       0xF012, 0xFBA5, 0xF011, 0xF89D, 0x6830

.close
```
